articles.title: I taste-tested 6 store-bought biscuits, and these are the only ones I'd buy again
articles.summary: We sampled offerings from Pillsbury, Trader Joe's, Annie's and more, so you don't spend your dough on something subpar.
articles.body:
Our experts independently review everything we recommend. If you buy through our links, we may earn commission.

Is there a more satisfying sound than popping open a can of biscuits? Sure, you could spend time cutting cold cubes of butter into flour, but when you want that flaky carbohydrate goodness fast, the best store-bought biscuits are a meal-saver. Just set the rounds of dough on a baking sheet , and in less than 20 minutes, voila . As a culinary school grad who has worked in restaurants, I know a good shortcut when I taste one. For this test, I tried six of the most popular ready-to-bake biscuit brands I could find. I prepared them on well-worn sheet pans in my oven, then sampled them while they were warm. The results were mostly tasty. But I tried just one canned biscuit I'd buy again — and I was truly surprised to find that the classic brand (hint, hint: It starts with a "pills" and ends with a "bury") was not the winner.

Serving size: 1 biscuit | Calories: 170 | Total fat: 6g

Hungry for a light, fluffy bread product that's fancier than a roll but not quite as cake-like as cornbread ? This pop-open-and-bake tube will not disappoint. They were the best canned biscuits I tried, baking to a gorgeous golden brown with a slightly crunchy top.

Made with USDA Organic-certified ingredients and without any preservatives, they have tender layers that pull apart easily. I appreciated that they maintained their hexagonal shape, a big help if you like to use biscuits for breakfast sandwiches . My only complaint is that they were a touch greasy, but they easily outdid the competition.

Fluffy, with a sturdy shape that would work well for breakfast sandwiches

I baked all six canned biscuit brands on my beloved NordicWare sheet pans . I set up a cooling rack, a spatula and some jam for tasting. As each tray came out of the oven, I let the biscuits cool on the sheet pan, and then I transferred them to a wire rack. While they were still warm, I split them open and tasted them plain and then with some jam, rating them on flakiness, flavor and appearance. The best store-bought biscuits I tried from Immaculate scored the highest in all categories and tasted just as delicious on their own as with a topping.

Trader Joe's Organic Biscuits : These were so similar to the Immaculate Baking biscuits that I wouldn't be surprised if those were the inspiration or even the manufacturer of the TJ biscuits. The shape, look and taste were almost identical.

Pillsbury Grands Original Biscuit Dough : If you grew up making these at home, you know how big, soft and fluffy they are. They're the same rounds as they were back then, but they didn't have as much texture or flavor as the Immaculate Baking ones. They are available in many variations, such as Buttermilk, Honey Butter, Sweet Hawaiian and more.

Annie's Organic Flaky Biscuits : The Annie's biscuits were close behind the Trader Joe's version. They, too, were a bit craggy on top, hexagonal in shape, and tender on the inside. I liked them, but they weren't my favorites.

Mason Dixie Buttermilk Biscuits : These were the only biscuits I tried that were fully cooked (you heat them in the oven) and sold in the freezer aisle. They are smaller in size and also the most expensive of all the brands. However, these were the biscuits that most closely resembled homemade biscuits, with a denser texture that's less buttery. They were the only biscuits that contained real butter and buttermilk — the others were made with palm oil.

Amazon Fresh Jumbo Flaky Biscuits: Unfortunately, the Amazon Fresh biscuits were a miss (they're also currently unavailable). The dough was an odd shade of yellow. They baked up to a puffy pillow, but there wasn't much flavor and they felt greasier than the others.

Amazon; background generated with ChatGPT

If you want to try your hand at making biscuits from scratch, these stainless steel cutters can help. They'll give you uniform rounds, and the handles make them a little easier to maneuver than, say, a drinking glass. This set of three gets a near-perfect 4.8-star rating from more than 3,000 shoppers — sweet!

Another essential for from-scratch biscuits, a pastry cutter can make or break your dough. The key to flaky baked goods is keeping the butter you mix into the flour cold. This stainless steel tool lets you blend the butter without actually touching it, so it doesn't warm up in your hands.

To help treats like biscuits, cookies and muffins cool evenly, a rack like this is a necessity. It allows airflow all around the food and helps prevent it from sticking to the pan.

Amazon; background generated/edited using ChatGPT

These have been my go-to sheet pans for almost 20 years, and they're our top pick after extensive testing. They heat evenly and are indestructible. I can clean them with hot water, a soapy sponge and elbow grease.

Don't be thrown by this tool's name — it's for way more than cooking fish. Because of its thin, flexible blade, this spatula works wonders sliding baked goods off a sheet pan. It easily cuts through any stuck-on bits of dough.

articles.title: Rare images of isolated Indigenous group in Brazil highlight threats
articles.summary: By Brendan O'Boyle Nov 17 (Reuters) - Rare images of an isolated group of Indigenous people emerging from a remote part of Brazil's Amazon rainforest have un...
articles.body:
Rare images of isolated Indigenous group in Brazil highlight threats

Nov 17 (Reuters) - Rare images of an isolated group of Indigenous people emerging from a remote part of Brazil's Amazon rainforest have underscored the threats facing them from loggers, hunters ‌and ranchers, advocates said on Tuesday.

Survival International, a UK-based Indigenous peoples' rights group, shared images on ‌Tuesday of what it said was a "historic encounter" a day earlier in a region of Brazil's northeastern Maranhão state between a government team ​and about 20 uncontacted Awá Indigenous people, who asked for food.

The rights organization defines uncontacted groups as Indigenous peoples who avoid contact with outsiders and have no permanent relationship with them even while being aware of the outside world.

"There hasn't been a similar approach like this with the Awá in recent history, certainly for some decades," said Survival International, ‌adding the people may have asked ⁠for food due to pressure from outsiders entering their territory.

Brazil's Indigenous affairs agency Funai said in a statement to Reuters that it was reviewing videos and accounts shared on ⁠social media showing isolated Awá people interacting with a village in the Araribóia Indigenous Land in Maranhão.

The agency said it has activated a contingency plan for contact situations with a focus on minimizing health risks for the Indigenous people. Funai ​also said ​the Brazilian state is not seeking contact with the ​group and its policy remains one of non-contact.

The ‌Awá are a Tupi-Guarani people in northwest Maranhão with some remaining in voluntary isolation, according to Funai.

Survival International said it released the images at the request of a group of Indigenous people known as the Guardians of the Amazon, which campaigns against illegal loggers and cattle ranchers. Reuters could not verify the location and date of the footage. No older versions were found posted online before November 17.

In recent decades, isolated Indigenous groups ‌across the Amazon, the world's largest rainforest, have come under threat ​from encroaching illegal miners, loggers and ranchers.

"The uncontacted Awá are under ​extreme pressure as intruders encroach from all ​sides of their territory, driving them into an ever-smaller island of the Amazon rainforest, surrounded ‌by destruction," Survival International's director, Caroline Pearce, ​said.

The organization has identified 196 uncontacted ​Indigenous groups across 10 countries in South America, Asia and the Pacific. It says almost 95% of these groups are in the Amazon, with 124 specifically in Brazil.

The Maranhão Indigenous people's organization COAPIMA said on Tuesday ​that the encounter with the Awá ‌people "underscores the importance of careful action by the responsible agencies, given the risks that unplanned ​contact can pose to isolated Indigenous populations, mainly through exposure to diseases and other threats to ​their integrity."

(Reporting by Brendan O'Boyle; Editing by Aurora Ellis)

articles.title: Santa Casa de Itapeva reúne prefeitos da região para pedir apoio | G1
articles.standfirst: Dívida soma R$ 47 milhões e pode acarretar no corte de atendimentos de diversos setores. Reunião contou com 15 prefeitos da região atendida pela unidade hospitalar.
articles.summary: A Santa Casa de Itapeva (SP) reuniu 15 prefeitos nesta quarta-feira (18) para pedir apoio financeiro. O hospital enfrenta uma dívida acumulada de R$ 47 milhões.
articles.body:
A diretoria da Santa Casa de Itapeva (SP) realizou, na tarde desta quarta-feira (18), uma reunião com 15 prefeitos das cidades atendidas pela unidade hospitalar para pedir apoio em meio a uma crise milionária que o hospital enfrenta.

Atualmente, a dívida da unidade soma R$ 47 milhões e, por isso, o local pode operar abaixo da capacidade oferecida e com cortes em atendimentos essenciais, como a redução de leitos na UTI adulto e as consultas via Iamspe. Veja a lista completa:

UTI adulto : dez leitos poderão ser retirados de funcionamento;

Hemodiálise e UTI neonatal : o projeto de expansão dos setores pode ser suspenso;

Porta referenciada : o hospital avalia que os atendimentos possam feitos somente por meio de encaminhamento, a partir de 1º de dezembro;

Iamspe : os atendimentos via convênio serão suspensos a partir de 25 de novembro.

Santa Casa de Itapeva (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

Durante a reunião, a gestão pediu apoio imediato ao custeio e um acordo regional, com contribuições, responsabilidades e prazos definidos em conjunto.

O prefeito de Nova Campina (SP), Antônio Isael de Oliveira Júnior (PSD), caracteriza a situação da unidade hospitalar como preocupante e diz que os representantes municipais pedirão ajuda aos governos estaduais e ao Governo Federal.

"Vamos nos reunir com os prefeitos para buscarmos ajuda. Precisamos colocar mais recursos na Santa Casa diante da prioridade de saúde. Não consigo nem imaginar a Santa Casa diminuindo atendimentos, porque isso impactaria diretamente a vida da população do sudoeste paulista. O nosso dever é garantir o atendimento prioritário da saúde", pontua.

Prefeito de Nova Campina, Antônio Isael (PSD) — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

De janeiro a outubro deste ano, a instituição, que é referência para 28 cidades, registrou um déficit de R$ 1,8 milhão no saldo do caixa. A gestão alega que os recursos repassados pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) não têm sido suficientes, devido à falta de reajustes na tabela nos últimos 20 anos.

Diante do déficit financeiro, o hospital afirma que precisou contratar um empréstimo de R$ 5 milhões para quitar o 13º salário dos funcionários e pagar fornecedores, cujos serviços estavam em atraso . Com a nova dívida, a parcela mensal, que era de R$ 500 mil, deve aumentar para R$ 700 mil.

O hospital recomenda que, com relação aos pacientes que tiverem procedimentos marcados por meio do Iamspe, seja consultada a situação do agendamento.

A TV TEM pediu uma nota de posicinamento à Secretaria Estadual da Saúde e aguarda retorno.

articles.title: MP investiga possíveis irregularidades em contratações de funcionários | G1
articles.standfirst: Inquérito civil vai apurar contratações temporárias, terceirizações e realização de concurso público em Riacho de Santana, no sudoeste do estado.
articles.summary: Inquérito civil vai apurar contratações temporárias, terceirizações e realização de concurso público em Riacho de Santana, no sudoeste do estado.
articles.body:
Prefeitura de Riacho de Santana, no sudoeste da Bahia — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

O Ministério Público da Bahia (MP-BA) instaurou um inquérito civil para investigar possíveis irregularidades nas contratações de funcionários pela Prefeitura de Riacho de Santana , no sudoeste da Bahia. A investigação abrange o período de 2021 a 2026 e inclui a atual gestão do prefeito João Vítor (PSD).

A abertura do procedimento foi publicada no Diário Oficial da Justiça de terça-feira (17). Segundo o documento, a investigação tem como objetivo apurar a política de contratação de pessoal adotada pelo município ao longo dos últimos seis anos.

Entre os pontos que serão analisados estão as contratações temporárias, a terceirização de serviços, os registros funcionais no sistema do Tribunal de Contas dos Municípios da Bahia (TCM-BA) e a realização de concursos públicos.

O inquérito foi instaurado pela Promotoria de Justiça de Riacho de Santana e assinado pelo promotor Antônio Eduardo Cunha Setúbal, que atua em substituição na unidade.

O g1 entrou em contato com a Prefeitura de Riacho de Santana, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Hegseth visita Venezuela e anuncia parceria militar com país | G1
articles.standfirst: Pete Hegseth se reuniu com a presidente interina Delcy Rodríguez em Caracas. Acordo prevê treinamento das Forças Armadas venezuelanas por militares americanos.
articles.summary: Pete Hegseth se reuniu com Delcy Rodríguez em Caracas. Visita ocorre em meio à aproximação entre os governos dos EUA e da Venezuela.
articles.body:
O secretário de Defesa dos Estados Unidos, Pete Hegseth, se reúne com a presidente interina da Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, no Palácio de Miraflores, em Caracas. — Foto: Foto: Palácio de Miraflores

Os Estados Unidos e a Venezuela assinaram um acordo para restabelecer as relações militares entre os dois países, abrangendo desde treinamento até compartilhamento de informações de inteligência, afirmou nesta quarta-feira (18) o secretário de Defesa dos EUA, Pete Hegseth.

Hegseth está na Venezuela e se reuniu com a presidente interina do país, Delcy Rodríguez. A televisão estatal exibiu imagens do secretário no palácio presidencial, em Caracas, ao lado de Delcy.

O secretário afirmou que, após a captura do presidente venezuelano Nicolás Maduro pelas Forças Armadas dos Estados Unidos, em janeiro, o país “passou de ameaça regional mais agressiva a um parceiro de segurança cooperativo”.

Hegseth disse que pretende ampliar a parceria militar entre os países e trabalhar em conjunto com as autoridades venezuelanas no combate ao tráfico de drogas. Ele também elogiou a “estreita cooperação” com Delcy Rodríguez, que permitiu às autoridades “estabilizar a Venezuela e livrá-la dos narcoterroristas de uma vez por todas”.

Rodríguez, por sua vez, também elogiou a oportunidade de fortalecer a parceria militar. “Espero que essa cooperação técnico-militar [...] possa alcançar seu nível mais elevado possível, para que [...] possamos enfrentar ameaças comuns”, afirmou

Segundo a presidente interina, o acordo permitirá aos Estados Unidos oferecer treinamento às Forças Armadas venezuelanas.

O Pentágono não apresentou imediatamente mais detalhes sobre a nova parceria.

Trump quer ampliar influência sobre a Venezuela

A viagem de Pete Hegseth ocorre em meio aos esforços do governo do presidente Donald Trump para ampliar sua influência no território venezuelano. Neste ano, os secretários do Interior e de Energia também estiveram no país para discutir o acesso às reservas de petróleo e minerais estratégicos.

O chefe das operações militares dos Estados Unidos na América Latina, general Francis Donovan, do Comando Sul das Forças Armadas americanas, também se reuniu com autoridades interinas da Venezuela pelo menos duas vezes neste ano.

Em agosto, Trump afirmou que Hegseth ajudou a negociar um acordo abrangente para que os Estados Unidos assumissem o controle de parte das reservas de petróleo venezuelanas .

EUA ampliam atuação militar na América Latina

As Forças Armadas americanas intensificaram a atenção à América Latina desde que Trump voltou à Casa Branca, no ano passado. O presidente republicano prometeu dar prioridade ao Hemisfério Ocidental e combater cartéis de drogas que atuam na região.

Com o objetivo declarado de reduzir a entrada de entorpecentes nos Estados Unidos e o número de mortes por overdose, forças americanas passaram a atacar embarcações que, segundo o governo Trump, transportam drogas no mar do Caribe e no leste do oceano Pacífico.

Pelo menos 240 pessoas morreram desde setembro de 2025, quando o governo americano começou a atacar alvos que classifica como "narcoterroristas". Autoridades dos Estados Unidos, no entanto, divulgaram poucas provas para sustentar as alegações de que as embarcações atingidas transportavam drogas.

Futuro político da Venezuela segue indefinido

A visita de Hegseth ocorre em um momento de incerteza sobre quem comandará a Venezuela nos próximos meses e anos.

Delcy Rodríguez, aliada de Maduro, assumiu o governo após a captura do então presidente . O período de mandato autorizado pela Justiça venezuelana terminou em julho, mas ela continua exercendo a chefia de Estado.

A líder da oposição, María Corina Machado, voltou recentemente à Venezuela depois de deixar o país . Ela estava no exílio após sete tentativas de retorno que, segundo ativistas da oposição, foram impedidas pelo governo.

O secretário de Estado dos Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, afirmou que o retorno seguro da política foi resultado de negociações para a reconciliação apoiadas pelo governo americano. Segundo ele, esse processo representa a melhor oportunidade que a Venezuela teve em três décadas para realizar eleições livres e justas e estabelecer uma democracia duradoura.

A ausência de uma data para a próxima eleição presidencial divide a opinião de venezuelanos sobre Trump. Embora muitos estejam aliviados com a saída de Maduro do poder, parte da população considera equivocada a decisão da Casa Branca de priorizar a recuperação da indústria petrolífera venezuelana em vez de adotar medidas voltadas à restauração da democracia.

O governo Trump afirma ter devolvido à Venezuela mais de US$ 12 bilhões, o equivalente a quase 99% da receita obtida com a venda de petróleo do país. A informação consta de um relatório divulgado neste mês e faz parte dos termos do acordo energético firmado com o governo de Rodríguez.

articles.title: Jetour anuncia fábrica no Brasil, investimento de R$ 400 milhões e novo SUV elétrico | G1
articles.standfirst: A montadora chinesa Jetour anunciou investimento adicional de R$ 400 milhões para produzir SUVs no Brasil a partir de 2027. A empresa também confirmou a chegada de um novo modelo elétrico ao país e pretende ampliar sua rede para 150 concessionárias até o fim do próximo ano.
articles.summary: A montadora chinesa Jetour anunciou investimento adicional de R$ 400 milhões para produzir SUVs no Brasil a partir de 2027.
articles.body:
Jetour investe R$ 400 milhões para produzir SUVs no Brasil e anuncia novo modelo — Foto: Reprodução/Jetour

A montadora chinesa Jetour anunciou nesta quarta-feira (18) um investimento adicional de R$ 400 milhões no Brasil para iniciar a produção nacional dos SUVs T1 e T2 em 2027.

Com o novo aporte, a empresa afirma que terá investido R$ 800 milhões no país , considerando outros R$ 400 milhões anunciados anteriormente.

Além da produção local, a companhia pretende lançar um novo modelo, o SUV T0, ampliar sua rede de concessionárias para 150 unidades até o fim de 2027 e desenvolver motores que funcionem com gasolina e etanol (tecnologia flex).

O anúncio foi feito por Ke Chuandeng, presidente da Jetour International, durante o Global Fan Festival, no Rio de Janeiro. Segundo o executivo, o local da fábrica será anunciado no primeiro trimestre de 2027.

A primeira etapa da produção brasileira terá os modelos T1 e T2. De acordo com a empresa, a escolha levou em consideração o planejamento da capacidade de fabricação e as possibilidades de parceria com fornecedores locais.

A montadora não informou quando exatamente as unidades começarão a ser produzidas.

Montadora chinesa Jetour investirá R$ 400 milhões para fabricar SUVs no Brasil em 2027 — Foto: Reprodução/Jetour

A Jetour também confirmou a chegada do T0 ao mercado brasileiro em 2027. O modelo será o veículo de entrada da linha T, ou seja, a opção inicial da família de SUVs da marca.

O carro será oferecido em duas versões: híbrida plug-in (que combina motor a combustão e elétrico e pode ser recarregada na tomada) e totalmente elétrica, sem motor a combustão. Esta última será o primeiro veículo 100% elétrico da marca no Brasil.

Para acompanhar o crescimento das vendas, a empresa estabeleceu a meta de chegar a 150 concessionárias no país até o fim de 2027 . A expansão também deverá envolver investimentos em assistência técnica, treinamento de profissionais e disponibilidade de peças.

Outra novidade prevista para o próximo ano é o lançamento de uma tecnologia de motorização flex , que permite abastecer o veículo com gasolina ou etanol . Segundo a montadora, o desenvolvimento considera as características do mercado brasileiro e o potencial de uso de biocombustíveis.

A empresa também afirmou que pretende avançar em sistemas de condução autônoma e tecnologias de assistência ao motorista, recursos que auxiliam o condutor em diferentes situações de trânsito.

Em seu primeiro ano de operação no país, a Jetour afirma ter vendido mais de 8 mil veículos e realizado seis lançamentos: S06 , T1 , T2 4x2, T2 XWD 4x4 , S08 e G700 .

Fundada em 2018, a montadora já vendeu mais de 2,4 milhões de veículos no mundo e está presente em mais de 100 países e regiões. A empresa também informou que possui 14 fábricas fora da China, em países como Indonésia, Malásia, Paquistão, Egito e Nigéria.

Até 2030, a companhia planeja ampliar sua estrutura internacional para 19 unidades produtivas fora da China, com capacidade para fabricar mais de 600 mil veículos por ano nesses mercados.

articles.title: Buracos e lama dificultam acesso a casas, trabalho e escolas em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: No Bairro Cristo Redentor, moradores relatam ônibus atolados, corridas por aplicativo canceladas e dificuldades para levar crianças à escola.
articles.summary: No Bairro Cristo Redentor, moradores relatam ônibus atolados, corridas por aplicativo canceladas e dificuldades para levar crianças à escola.
articles.body:
Buracos, lama e enxurradas têm dificultado a rotina dos moradores do Bairro Cristo Redentor, em Campo Grande . O problema, que se agrava nos dias de chuva, impede o acesso a casas, atrasa trabalhadores e prejudica o transporte de crianças até as escolas.

Ao g1 , moradores afirmam que os problemas são antigos e continuam sem solução, apesar das reclamações feitas às autoridades. Procurada, a Secretaria Municipal de Infraestrutura e Serviços Públicos (Sisep) informou que fará o patrolamento das vias do bairro e, em seguida, o cascalhamento das principais ruas.

Outras vias também serão incluídas no cronograma de cascalhamento, conforme a necessidade identificada pelas equipes técnicas. Enquanto a situação não é resolvida, os moradores enfrentam transtornos diários.

Morador da Rua Kanga Rosa há quatro anos, o marmorista Eroilcon da Silva Santos conta que precisa mudar o caminho para chegar em casa. Nos dias de chuva, motoristas de aplicativo evitam entrar no bairro por causa das condições das ruas.

Nesta quarta-feira (18), Eroilcon teve três corridas de aplicativo canceladas porque os motoristas não conseguiram chegar à casa dele. Para conseguir transporte, os moradores precisam marcar o embarque em outras ruas, onde os carros ainda conseguem passar.

"Carro atola, aplicativo não vem, às vezes nem os ônibus passam. Está muito difícil a situação aqui no bairro", desabafa.

Rua coberta de lama no bairro Cristo Redentor, em Campo Grande — Foto: Débora Ricalde

Nos dias secos, a poeira também incomoda. Segundo Eroilcon, os moradores já procuraram as autoridades e espalharam cartazes com a frase "O Cristo Redentor pede socorro" , mas não receberam resposta.

Mesmo morando a uma quadra da Avenida Três Barras, uma das principais da região, Eroilcon afirma que tem dificuldade para chegar em casa.

Buracos dificultam trajeto de crianças até a escola

Os buracos e a lama também dificultam o caminho de crianças até a escola. Na Rua Lourenço Alves da Costa, a técnica de enfermagem Célia Alves Barbosa conta que costuma levar a filha de carro ou bicicleta, mas os buracos e a água acumulada tornam o percurso difícil e perigoso.

A situação é ainda mais difícil para mães que precisam levar mais de uma criança à escola. Célia conta que uma amiga transporta três crianças de bicicleta. Uma delas estuda na Escola Municipal de Educação Infantil (Emei) Zacarias Vieira de Andrade.

Segundo Célia, algumas crianças já faltaram às aulas por causa das condições das ruas. Ela conta que precisou ajudar uma mãe a levar a filha para fazer uma prova porque a rua estava em más condições.

"Prejudica as crianças, pessoas que trabalham. Às vezes, os ônibus atrasam e as pessoas têm horário para chegar ao serviço. A gente precisa de um olhar mais cuidadoso com a região", afirma.

Célia conta que um ônibus já ficou atolado perto da casa dela. Segundo a moradora, três linhas de ônibus atendem a região, mas os buracos e a lama dificultam a passagem dos veículos.

A filha de Célia, Isadora Alves Brito, conta que já ficou com os pés sujos de lama ao ir de bicicleta para a escola. A menina também teme sofrer acidentes por causa dos buracos.

"Eu acho que a prefeita podia botar uma placa para tomar cuidado, porque tem buraco e tem muito acidente caindo de bike", sugere a menina.

Parquinho cheio de lama, no bairro Cristo Redentor em Campo Grande — Foto: Débora Ricalde

O acúmulo de água da chuva também preocupa os moradores. A advogada Verônica Chami conta que, durante os temporais, a força da enxurrada impede a passagem de veículos e pedestres.

"O bairro, quando chove, é aquela enxurrada constante. Você não pode sair de casa. É um rio mesmo, correndo", descreve.

Segundo Verônica, mesmo depois que a chuva diminui, a água continua saindo de alguns terrenos e mantém as ruas molhadas.

Os moradores cobram melhorias nas ruas para garantir a passagem segura de motoristas, pedestres e ônibus.

articles.title: South Korea is offering $75,000 rewards to help catch people cheating with AI in its most important exam
articles.summary: South Korea is combating AI cheating in the national high-stakes university entrance exam by introducing bounties and inspecting glasses.
articles.body:
South Korea is cracking down with a $75,000 reward to catch AI exam cheaters.

The government also plans to use the national emergency alert system to catch hidden phones.

It comes after the top scorer in a tax accountant exam confessed to cheating using AI.

South Korea is cracking down on AI exam cheating by offering huge bounties to catch somebody breaking the rules.

President Lee Jae-myung said in a Tuesday X post that he's introducing a system with rewards of at least 100 million won, or $75,000.

The announcement came two days before Suneung — a high-stakes university entrance exam. It brings such immense pressure that corporate offices open an hour late to clear the roads, while airplanes are grounded during the 35-minute English listening test to minimize noise.

But the government is scrambling to prevent cheating after a recent scandal in South Korea's certified tax-accountant exam.

Han Won-seok, the top scorer, admitted Sunday on his lawyer's YouTube account that he had photographed questions with a microcamera, sent them to AI, and checked the answers on a smartphone. He got just one question wrong out of 160.

"Cheating on exams using advanced equipment is no different from stealing the scores of hundreds of thousands of examinees who worked hard," President Lee wrote on X.

He said authorities had agreed with AI companies to obtain records of users who photograph exam questions during the testing period.

Prime Minister Han Seong-sook also announced a host of anti-cheating checks.

The government is planning to send an emergency alert before the exam starts, aiming to expose phones that students failed to hand in.

Any electronic device found in a student's possession but not submitted to a proctor will automatically be treated as cheating, Han said.

Students will also have their glasses inspected before every session to identify AI-enabled devices. Proctors will place stickers over every button on their clothes to prevent hidden cameras, while students will be asked to roll up their sleeves for checks and leave their bags outside exam rooms.

Authorities are also pursuing a proposal to increase the ban on retaking the Suneung after cheating from one year to 10 years.

And it plans to seek criminal investigations into cheating with smart devices, which could carry a sentence of up to five years in prison for obstructing official duties by deception.

"If anyone is considering cheating on the exam," Lee wrote, "please do not ruin your life by hoping for a lucky break."

articles.title: Billy Allison guilty of murdering Matthew O'Gara on Lichfield bar dancefloor
articles.summary: Billy Allison punched Matthew O'Gara in the neck at a bar in Lichfield in May.
articles.body:
A member of activist group Raise The Colours has been found guilty of murdering a pub landlord who died after being punched in the neck on the dancefloor at a bar.

Matthew O'Gara, 44, was attacked by Billy Allison at Rico and Loren bar in Lichfield, Staffordshire, on 24 May.

Allison was also found guilty of causing grievous bodily harm with intent to O'Gara's friend Adam Cooper, 62, who was punched twice and was left with a fractured eye socket and nose.

O'Gara, who ran The Plough on the outskirts of Lichfield, suffered two broken bones and a split artery in his neck, which caused a massive bleed and rendered him unconscious until he died in hospital two days later, Stafford Crown Court heard.

The trial was told the punch could be heard over the bar's DJ sound system.

Allison, who had been drunk and had taken cocaine during the day, had admitted manslaughter ahead of the trial, but denied murder.

He appeared shocked by the verdict, sighing and holding his head in his hands and seeming to cry as he left the dock without being granted permission by the judge.

"While the conclusion of the court proceedings has brought a measure of justice, it can never replace the loss we have suffered or bring Matthew back," O'Gara's family said in a statement issued following the verdict.

"Our heartfelt thanks also go to Matthew's friends, whose unwavering support has meant so much to us during this ordeal.

"He remains deeply loved, will be forever missed, and will always hold a special place in our hearts."

Det Insp Lisa Holland, who led the investigation, said the attack was wholly unprovoked and came without warning.

"I would like to pay tribute to Matthew's family for the dignity, courage and patience they have shown throughout this difficult process," she said.

"While today's verdict cannot bring Matthew back, I hope it provides his family and friends with a measure of justice and reassurance that Allison has been held accountable for his actions."

The jury of seven men and five women were not told during the trial of Allison's link to Raise The Colours.

They heard the defendant had been drinking in Lichfield with his partner Charlotte Dean and friends, including fellow Colours members Ryan Bridge and Ben Cullen, on the day of the attack.

In his closing speech to the jury on Monday, Timothy Hannam KC, prosecuting, said there was a "thread of events" leading to O'Gara's death, which began with the victim shaking Bridge's hand on the dancefloor.

"A handshake that Matthew O'Gara crossed the bar and dancefloor to make, but one that it seems Ryan Bridge did not particularly welcome," Hannam added.

Asked during the trial by Hannam why he had punched O'Gara, Allison said: "It was just a moment of madness, I was very drunk."

He added: "I just don't have an explanation for why... I had a bit of a sense I was being looked at, in my drunken state, maybe I was a touch paranoid.

"I didn't intentionally punch him that hard."

He denied having been aware of the handshake between O'Gara and Bridge when the victim arrived on the dancefloor, after which Bridge appeared to roll his eyes, the prosecution said.

Allison also said he could not remember what he and Bridge were talking about when they appeared to have some "exchanges" seconds before the defendant took two steps over to O'Gara and attacked him.

After the attack, Allison fled the bar through a back entrance with Cullen, before the pair swapped T-shirts and Allison covered his face as they walked through the city.

Allison and Cullen were next seen on CCTV at about 01:00 in parkland, before later reappearing at the Cathedral Hotel in Beacon Street, where Cullen had been booked to stay the night.

The trial heard eyewitnesses describe Allison, who had been drinking at several bars and pubs in Lichfield with his group, as "almost frothing, as if wanting a fight and manic, as if he was on something".

Hannam said 6ft 5ins (1.95m) Allison delivered "powerful boxer punches" to two men who were smaller than him in the space of around six seconds, "demolishing" both of them.

In his evidence to the court, Cooper described the force of the attack as like being hit by a "sledgehammer".

Allison is due to be sentenced on 5 January.

articles.title: World waits as Trump, Xi and Putin prepare for high-stakes meeting
articles.summary: SHENZHEN, China — What these three men might decide has the potential to reverberate across the globe.
articles.body: SHENZHEN, China — What these three men might decide has the potential to reverberate across the globe. But the spectacle of President Donald Trump’s meeting with rivals Russia’s Vladimir Putin and China’s Xi Jinping may be what delivers the defining image. Before a word uttered in English, Russian or Mandarin, comparisons have already been drawn with the Yalta Conference of 1945, in which President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin sat down to carve up the postwar world. On Thursday, Trump, Putin and Xi will gather on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen. They will project power, with Trump governing the world’s largest economy, Putin the biggest nuclear arsenal, and Xi the largest standing army and manufacturing sector. Allies, whose futures may hinge on the whims of these three personalities, would be forgiven for worrying because, as the saying goes, “If you are not at the table, you are on the menu.” The meeting itself represents a major shift from Washington’s post-Cold War policy of driving a wedge between Moscow and Beijing, said Ali Wyne, a senior adviser for U.S.-China relations at the International Crisis Group, a think tank based in Belgium. Now, Trump and Putin “are currying favor with President Xi,” he added. “The symbolism is going to be very powerful.” Trump says he wants to discuss nuclear disarmament, the Iran war, economics and trade. On Monday, he added his “favorite subject, Ukraine,” contradicting White House officials who had said just days earlier that Russia’s war would not feature in the discussions. Trump has previously called for a new nuclear arms control deal — that includes China as well as Russia — after the final deal between Washington and Moscow, named New START, lapsed in February. “When the leaders of the three largest nuclear powers sit down to discuss how to reduce the proliferation of these weapons, that is always important,” said John B. Emerson, a former U.S. diplomat who served as ambassador to Germany under President Barack Obama. Trump, who has also sought to resume talks with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un over his sanctioned nuclear program, “sees denuclearization as a legacy deal,” said Craig Singleton, a China expert at the Washington-based Foundation for Defense of Democracies. “He’s betting that his relationships can get leaders into a room that other presidents couldn’t assemble,” he said in written comments. A bigger accomplishment, Singleton said, would be getting Beijing to join real talks on nuclear arms reduction, although he called that possibility a “long shot.” China is reluctant to engage on the subject when its estimated nuclear arsenal of 600 warheads, though growing rapidly, is still eclipsed by the more than 5,000 each held by the U.S. and Russia. Moscow, meanwhile, has made clear that it wants Ukraine on the agenda although not at the table. This comes as the U.S. and Russian officials have called for negotiations over Europe’s wider security arrangements to be part of any lasting peace settlement — something that deeply alarms long-standing American allies. This arrangement has also worried Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said last month that “we really don’t want this to turn into ‘Yalta 2, 3, 4’ with a redistribution of influence.” Yalta saw the great powers of the day carve up Berlin into occupied zones, sowing the seeds for communist control of Eastern Europe and the beginning of the Cold War. Senior U.S. officials told reporters ahead of Trump’s trip that the Ukraine war was a separate “track” that China is not part of and that it would not be “appropriate” for the three leaders to discuss it. Beijing has also signaled its reluctance to discuss Ukraine without European leaders at the table. Even if Trump, Putin and Xi don’t decide anything on Ukraine at their meeting, the fact that it’s happening at all only reinforces Ukraine’s suspicion “that Washington is increasingly negotiating with Moscow to the detriment of Kyiv, or perhaps even siding with Moscow,” Wyne said. China, which says this week’s trilateral meeting has “groundbreaking significance,” has nonetheless tried to manage expectations. Da Wei, director of the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University in Beijing, said he didn’t expect anything concrete to come from the meeting but that it was a “starting point” that could promote international stability. “No matter we like them or not, these three leaders and these three countries are major shapers of the international order,” he said in an interview Wednesday. “So for that reason, I think the meeting among the three is a good thing.” Jennifer Jett and Janis Mackey Frayer reported from Shenzhen, and Alexander Smith from Londn.

articles.title: Former world boxing champion is in ICE custody amid calls for his release
articles.summary: Jorge Linares, 41, is originally from Venezuela and earned championship titles in three different weight categories throughout his two-decade-long career.
articles.body: Former Venezuelan world boxing champion Jorge Linares remained in ICE custody Wednesday after immigration authorities arrested him in Texas three days ago, as friends and colleagues in the boxing community advocated for his release. Throughout his two-decade career, Linares won 47 of his 56 bouts and held world titles at lightweight, ​featherweight and super featherweight. Known to his fans as “El Niño de Oro” (The Golden Boy), Linares, 41, retired in 2023. Linares, who lives in Miami, was in El Paso to attend the ProBox TV Boxing event at the El Paso County Coliseum, NBC affiliate KTSM of El Paso reported. On Sunday, after he was arrested at the El Paso International Airport, Linares alerted his followers on X, writing in a Spanish-language post, “ICE has me held in El Paso, Texas. It’s crazy.” A spokesperson for ICE told NBC News on Wednesday that U.S. Border Patrol agents and ICE officers arrested Linares because he’s not authorized to be in the country. According to ICE, Linares first came to the U.S. on Oct. 26, 2023, “with permission to stay for a temporary period, but in defiance of our nation’s laws, he overstayed his welcome.” Wilner & O’Reilly, the law firm representing Linares, said in a statement Tuesday that their client “is authorized to be in the United States and he has cooperated fully with immigration authorities.” “We are in communication with ICE and are working to resolve this matter as quickly as possible. Immigration matters follow established procedures, and those procedures take time,” the law firm said. “We are confident in Mr. Linares’s position and ask his fans, the press and the public for patience in the meantime.” Online ICE records show Linares is being held in the El Paso Processing Center. The ICE spokesperson said he will remain in ICE custody pending removal proceedings. The ICE spokesperson added that having “a pending application or work authorization does not confer legal status in the United States.” His friends in the boxing community in Miami are advocating for his release. Monica Schloeter, owner of the boxing gym Brawlerz Box, said Linares works out at her gym at least three times a week and serves as mentor to boxers of all ages. “He’s like family to us now. He shares Christmas, birthdays and New Year’s with us. So, this has really hit us hard,” Schloeter told Noticias Telemundo in Spanish. “Everyone here loves Jorge. He always comes and talks to the children. He mentors all the groups, from the youngest to the oldest. He’s a wonderful person. He always wants to help everyone.” The World Boxing Association is also calling for Linares’ release. Gilberto Mendoza Jr., president of the World Boxing Association, described himself as a father figure to Linares in an interview with Noticias Telemundo on Tuesday. Mendoza said he is in contact with Linares and his family. “He’s fine. He’s surrounded by people who are treating him well, mostly other Latinos and officers who recognized him.” “Miami is his home and we are waiting for him,” Schloeter said in Spanish.

articles.title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper
articles.summary: Information sent to the Times newspaper by the General Medical Council included summaries of complaints alleging antisemitism and Islamophobia against doctors.
articles.body:
The doctors' regulator the General Medical Council (GMC) has apologised after it mistakenly sent information about more than 220 doctors to a national newspaper.

The information included summaries of complaints alleging antisemitism or Islamophobia against the doctors.

For some of the medics involved, it was only when the GMC alerted them to the data breach that they discovered a complaint had been made about them.

The GMC says it is "very sorry" for the incident and has reported itself to the Information Commissioner's Office.

The GMC - an independent body that regulates doctors, physician associates and anaesthesia associates to protect patient safety - sent the information about 223 doctors to a journalist at the Times newspaper.

While no names were revealed, GMC identification numbers were included, which would easily allow doctors to be found on the regulator's register.

Some doctors have also raised concerns that their ethnicity was included in the data breach.

All the medics involved have been the subject of a complaint involving either antisemitism or Islamophobia, dating from the Hamas attack on Israel in October 2023 to September 2026.

The GMC says it has a legal and statutory responsibility to investigate such claims.

Meanwhile, the Times is understood to have promised not to make any of the leaked details public, but has said it will not delete the leaked information.

A spokesman for the doctor's trade union, the British Medical Association (BMA), condemned the leak.

"The BMA is aware that a number of doctors have received communication from the GMC to say that it erroneously sent personal identifiable data about them to the Times newspaper when responding to a media request," it said.

"The GMC must take action to ensure such a breach never occurs again."

The BMA said it would look at ways to support members affected and urged them to make contact via their website.

A doctors' campaign group, The Doctors' Association UK (DAUK), called for an independent investigation into the leak.

"If a doctor sent identifiable patient information to a newspaper, they could expect to be referred to the GMC," said Dr Matt Kneale, DAUK co-chairman.

"The GMC should hold itself to the same standard of confidentiality it expects from doctors. It owes every affected doctor a clear account of what it sent, how that happened and what it is doing to get the information deleted."

The doctors' regulator says around a fifth (20%) of the complaints made have already resulted in some sanction related to antisemitism, including two doctors who have been struck off the medical register.

Just over a quarter of complaints over Islamophobia - 26% - have led to disciplinary action.

But other complaints were closed, having failed to reach the threshold for investigation.

The GMC said it had contacted the doctors affected to explain what had happened, to apologise and provide information and support.

A spokesperson added: "We recognise the concern this will cause to both those impacted personally and other registrants and we are very sorry this happened.

"Our priority continues to be supporting those affected and taking steps to reduce the impact of this incident."

articles.title: Donald Trump meets ‘longtime friend’ Imelda Marcos during Philippines visit
articles.summary: Trump told Philippine President Marcos he knew his parents ‘very well’.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump reunited with longtime friend Imelda Marcos, the widow of an ousted dictator and mother of the incumbent Philippine president, Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

Trump got to know the Philippine first couple while partying in New York decades ago.

Wednesday’s brief encounter happened at Manila’s Malacanang presidential palace, where Trump was received with a red-carpet welcome and full military honours.

On Tuesday evening, before a speech to Asian leaders, Trump praised Marcos and his parents, saying, “I just don’t wanna date myself, but I knew your parents very well,” adding that Marcos Jr had “good genetics”.

Imelda Marcos now 97, was known for her lavish lifestyle and vast collection of expensive shoes accumulated while her husband, Ferdinand Marcos, was in power as president for more than 20 years, at a time when many Filipinos lived in poverty-stricken conditions.

Since Marcos was ousted in the 1986 “people power” revolution, Imelda has faced several charges of embezzlement, corruption and tax evasion.

Once seated inside the sprawling palace for their meeting, Trump told Marcos their countries’ people have a lot in common and stressed “architectural tastes”.

“I love what you’ve done here,” Trump said, referring to the palace. “You’ve done a fantastic job.”

Marcos said he sent Trump a delivery from Jollibee, the Philippines’ biggest homegrown fast-food chain, so he could have a “taste of Manila” during his short stay in the capital.

Trump arrived in Manila on Tuesday night to join leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) at their annual summit meetings.

On Wednesday, Trump shook hands and exchanged greetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin before a group photo at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China.

articles.title: DOJ charges former Penn State student at center of fraternity drug bust
articles.summary: The Justice Department on Wednesday filed criminal charges against a former Pennsylvania State University fraternity brother who prosecutors say was at the center of a drug trafficking ring at the university.
articles.body: The Justice Department on Wednesday filed criminal charges against a former Pennsylvania State University fraternity brother who prosecutors say was at the center of a drug trafficking ring at the university. Agostino Abbatiello, 24, of Westbury, New York, was charged with one count of conspiracy to distribute cocaine and six counts of distributing cocaine, the Justice Department said in a news release. The maximum penalty under federal law for this offense is life in prison, according to the DOJ. Federal prosecutors alleged that between January 2023 and December 2024, Abbatiello was a “major supplier” of cocaine to fraternities at Penn State. Abbatiello, a former member of Sigma Chi, sold cocaine in bulk quantities on numerous occasions to the Sigma Chi and Delta Upsilon fraternities, often as much as a kilogram at a time, according to officials. Abbatiello purchased cocaine from suppliers in Philadelphia and New York, officials said. He also recruited others to assist him in obtaining his supply and transporting it to State College, where he used other fraternity brothers and pledges to package the illicit drugs for resale, according to officials. “This defendant was the top rung of the ladder for a high-level drug trafficking ring that supplied cocaine to Penn State University students,” Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday said in the release. A lawyer for Abbatiello did not immediately return a request for comment. Wyatt DuBois, a spokesperson for Penn State, referred NBC News to the Justice Department. The university has previously said it has not officially recognized Sigma Chi for years. Sigma Chi’s national organization said it suspended its state chapter after the allegations were made public. Hours after the DOJ charged Abbatiello, Penn State announced that it will no longer recognize the other fraternity alleged to be involved in the alleged drug ring, Delta Upsilon. Penn State said it found evidence that Delta Upsilon members committed acts of hazing that “included extensive control over daily activities, acts of servitude, sleep deprivation, physical punishment, intimidation, humiliation and threats of additional harm.” A representative for Delta Upsilon’s national body did not immediately return a request for comment. In August, state authorities had already arrested and charged Abbatiello in connection with the alleged scheme; he was charged with felony corrupt organizations, conspiracy and dealing in proceeds of unlawful activity. Thirteen other people were arrested in connection with the alleged drug scheme, including current and former students and the father of a former student. Abbatiello posted bail set at $250,000 in connection with his state charges and was released from Pennsylvania detention as he awaits further proceedings.

articles.title: Trump cannot deter Xi and Putin’s nuclear goals with a strategy designed for just one
articles.summary: President Donald Trump should take a strong position when he meets Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in China with nuclear arms control possibly on the agenda.
articles.body: President Donald Trump’s visit to China includes meeting with America’s foremost nuclear peer competitors: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Nuclear arms control is likely on their agenda. The United States must tread carefully here. This meeting comes at a consequential moment, as the New START Treaty – which restricted Russia’s and America’s nuclear arsenals – expired earlier this year. We cannot afford to simply recreate an agreement designed for a world that no longer exists. When New START was first negotiated in 2010, the United States operated in a very different strategic reality. Nuclear competition was primarily between the United States and Russia. Sixteen years later, the world looks very different. TRUMP KICKS OFF HIGH-STAKES ASIA TRIP WITH XI, PUTIN MEETINGS LOOMING ON WORLD STAGE Today, America faces two major nuclear competitors simultaneously. China is rapidly expanding and modernizing its nuclear forces, constructing new missile silos, fielding advanced delivery systems and developing capabilities that increasingly threaten the United States and our allies. That is why New START reached the end of its usefulness. An arms control agreement that limits the United States and Russia while leaving China’s growing nuclear arsenal unconstrained is no longer sufficient. America cannot and should not design our nuclear forces around outdated assumptions. CHINA, RUSSIA, IRAN AND NORTH KOREA FORM 'AXIS OF AGGRESSORS' THAT COULD OVERWHELM US, BOOK WARNS Unfortunately, neither China nor Russia has demonstrated the commitment necessary for meaningful arms control. China seeks the influence of a great power while refusing the responsibility that comes with it, including meaningful nuclear dialogue. I saw this firsthand during an official Senate delegation trip to China earlier this year: Chinese officials demurred when I raised this topic directly. Russia, meanwhile, has repeatedly violated or undermined arms control commitments and suspended its participation in New START in 2023, making the agreement even weaker. Given Russia’s track record and China’s reluctance, I do not believe arms control alone will adequately address the threat we face today. We can continue pursuing meaningful discussion, but it would be naïve to assume negotiations will succeed. Arms control can complement deterrence, but it cannot substitute for it. RUSSIA READIES NEW 500-MILE MISSILE AS WEAPON EXPERT WARNS OF 'TERMINAL END GAME SURPRISES' That means we must maintain the right quantity and mix of weapons to confront Russia’s advantage in nonstrategic nuclear weapons and China’s rapid expansion. Recognizing this, the bipartisan Congressional Commission on the Strategic Posture of the United States concluded in 2023 that America’s currently planned nuclear force posture is insufficient for the threat environment of the coming decade. RUSSIA IS HELPING CHINA CLOSE GAP WITH US FORCES AMID TAIWAN TENSIONS, WARNS LONGTIME MILITARY LEADER Deterring two nuclear competitors may require a larger and more flexible force than we planned for in 2010. That is why, as chair of the Strategic Forces Subcommittee on the Senate Armed Services Committee, I believe we must strengthen every leg of the nuclear triad. An arms control agreement that limits the United States and Russia while leaving China’s growing nuclear arsenal unconstrained is no longer sufficient. Our bomber force, which provides visible, flexible and recallable deterrence, is aging and stretched thin. In a world with two peer nuclear adversaries, the United States needs at least 200 next-generation stealth bombers to maintain readiness and strategic flexibility. The Air Force’s original plan for at least 100 B-21s is not enough to counter Chinese and Russian threats. AIR FORCE SAYS TWO ADVANCED STEALTHY AIRCRAFT ARE AHEAD OF SCHEDULE, WITH FIRST DELIVERY SET FOR 2027 At sea, the Columbia-class submarine will be the backbone of America’s second-strike capability. The United States must seriously evaluate whether the planned number of submarines is adequate for a future defined by simultaneous Russian and Chinese threats. We must also expand our arsenal of theater nuclear forces, which will be vital for managing the risk of regional nuclear conflicts. On land, we must completely replace our aging intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) system, which dates back to the 1960s. The new Sentinel ICBM program requires new infrastructure, launch facilities and command centers. And we must do this while sustaining our old Minuteman III ICBMs, which we need to maintain deterrence until the new Sentinel ICBM program is complete. RUSSIA’S QUIETER NUCLEAR SUBMARINES THREATEN NATO, FORMER COMMANDER WARNS The credibility of American deterrence also matters beyond our borders. Our nuclear capabilities remind our allies that the United States can and will meet our security commitments. As nuclear threats grow in Asia, South Korea and Japan are wondering whether they need nuclear deterrents of their own. A credible American deterrent reassures our friends and reduces incentive for further nuclear proliferation. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION The strength of our nuclear forces and hope for meaningful arms control are closely connected. Negotiations should not replace investing in our capabilities, and any future agreement must be grounded in the threats America actually faces. But preventing one requires realistic arms control backed by an American deterrent strong enough that no adversary ever doubts our ability to defend ourselves and our allies. articles.title: Leicester City split with sponsor after porn actress complaints
articles.summary: A fans group had complained after BC Game appointed a porn actress as a brand ambassador.
articles.body:
Leicester City have parted ways with their main shirt sponsor after the gambling firm appointed a porn actress as an ambassador.

BC Game - which was named as a sponsor for the League One side at the start of the 2024-25 season - named Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador earlier this month .

The online gambling company posted a video of Elfie and a delivery driver on social media, with the caption: "Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin."

The club, which had faced criticism from fans' group The Foxes Trust, said it had reached a "mutual agreement" to ends its partnership with the firm and fans who had bought shirts in the past 28 days could exchange them.

BC Game announced its new ambassador at the beginning of the month, prompting the trust to state: "Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people.

"Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?"

On Wednesday the club issued a statement which said it and the sponsor had "reached a mutual agreement to conclude our commercial partnership with immediate effect".

It also thanked the firm for the "constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement".

The statement confirmed an "enhanced returns policy" where it would accept BC Game branded shirts bought since 21 October for exchange or refund even if they had been worn or personalised.

articles.title: MIKE DAVIS: Washington is strangling the humble radio
articles.summary: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr could scrap 1996 radio ownership caps that threaten emergency alerts, high school sports and farm reports in small towns.
articles.body: When tornado sirens sound, high school and college basketball games tip off or farmers need the latest crop and weather report, Americans still turn to local radio. Yet Washington keeps imposing last-century rules on the stations that provide them. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr now has a chance to deliver real reform, not for a favored industry but for the communities that depend on radio. Congress set these ownership caps in 1996. This was when dial-up internet was cutting-edge, CDs were king, the iPod did not exist and satellite radio had not yet launched. CDs are dead. The iPod is gone. A hometown station now battles Spotify, SiriusXM, YouTube, podcasts, social media and the largest technology companies on earth. Those national giants reach nearly every American with a smartphone, and no federal rule caps their presence in any single town. DAVID MARCUS: CONGRESS SET TO PROTECT AM RADIO AND AMERICAN DISCOURSE The station down the road — warning where the storm is headed, carrying the high school game and reporting livestock and grain prices — faces tighter federal limits under rules from a bygone era. Carr is right to call this regulatory nostalgia. The question is simple: Will Washington let small stations build the scale to survive or protect bureaucratic boxes while listeners lose the service they count on? STEVE FORBES: REGULATORS RISK DESTROYING LOCAL TV BY BLOCKING KEY MEDIA MERGER The current framework uses a sliding scale. Even in the largest markets, one company generally may own no more than eight stations and no more than five in either AM or FM. Smaller markets face stricter caps still. The rule pretends radio lives in a sealed-off world that online platforms and endless digital choices never touch. Today's FCC should recognize those Big Tech competitors and scrap this relic. Nobody in the school pickup line or tractor cab cares about federal categories. They choose between a local morning show, a podcast, satellite radio and a streaming playlist, often within the same commute. That is one marketplace, and every competitor in it fights for the same listeners and advertising dollars. CARS FLIPPED, SCHOOL DEVASTATED AS VIOLENT TWISTER RIPS THROUGH POPULAR CITY These caps threaten the local service they claim to protect. Newsrooms, towers, backup generators, engineers and on-air talent cost serious money, and a standalone station often cannot shoulder that burden by itself. Sharing those costs across stations can keep emergency alerts live, ballgames on the dial and agricultural reports reaching the people who need them. Deny that scale, and Washington risks shutting down a vital source of news for rural and small-town America. When twisters strike, floods rise, wildfires spread or cellular networks fail, free over-the-air radio becomes the lifeline. If the power goes out, a battery-powered receiver still works when nothing else does. Broadcasters on the ground know the roads, schools, shelters and hospitals. Obsolete rules should not push those voices toward silence. BIPARTISAN LAWMAKERS WANT TO STRIP BIG TECH'S LEGAL IMMUNITY THAT CAN SHIELD SOCIAL MEDIA COMPANIES Critics will shout "monopoly," but they aim at the wrong target. Ending arbitrary caps would not eliminate FCC review of station purchases or block action against actual competitive harm, and the Justice Department would keep its antitrust authority over radio deals. Reform would stop the government from treating another locally operated station as more dangerous than a nationwide platform with enormous reach. Conservatives cannot trust federal bureaucrats to manufacture "viewpoint diversity" by counting how many microphones a private company may own. Genuine diversity comes from voices with deep roots in their communities — voices that know the county fair, the homecoming rivalry, the weekend forecast and the needs of family farms and small businesses. The First Amendment is safer in the hands of listeners than regulators. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Chairman Carr should follow the evidence and eliminate local ownership caps. Let broadcasters invest, compete and keep homegrown voices on the air for another generation. Washington must stop strangling radio before another town loses its local voice, its last dependable source of information.

articles.title: Teens say AI surveillance system at Baltimore school mistook Doritos bag for a gun
articles.summary: A group of Black teenagers said in a lawsuit that they were handcuffed and searched by Baltimore police officers outside their high school after an AI surveillance system mistook a bag of potato chips for a gun.
articles.body: A group of Black teenagers said in a lawsuit that they were handcuffed and searched by Baltimore police officers outside their high school after an AI surveillance system mistook a bag of potato chips for a gun. Lawyers for the teens filed a civil lawsuit Tuesday in the Circuit Court for Baltimore County alleging that the teens’ civil rights were violated during the Oct. 20, 2025, incident at Kenwood High School. The four students were waiting outside the school around 6:30 p.m. for a parent to pick them up from football practice, the suit states. One of the teens was eating a bag of Cool Ranch Doritos that his coach gave him. Without warning, the teens were surrounded by at least six Baltimore County Police Department officers, many of them with their guns drawn, the suit says. The officers “forced the students to their knees on the concrete” and then handcuffed and searched them, the suit alleges. Only after the search was the group told that Omnilert, an AI surveillance system used by the school, prompted the police response, according to the lawsuit. Omnilert uses a weapon-detection system that scans security camera footage for firearms. According to the lawsuit, the alert was canceled by school and police officials minutes after it was determined there was no gun, but the school’s principal did not relay that information. Instead, it says the principal took a screenshot of video footage from Omnilert and sent it to the school resource officer, who forwarded it to the police department, prompting the response. “This should have never been escalated to the police. It simply should not have happened, and we filed this lawsuit to prevent this from ever happening again,” Leah Frazier, an attorney for the teens, said in a statement. The lawsuit alleges unreasonable search and seizure, false imprisonment and negligence. It names Omnilert, the school, its principal and the Baltimore County Police Department as defendants. Omnilert and the police department said they was unable to comment on pending litigation. The school district and the principal did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Wednesday. In a November 2025 report, the Maryland Office of the Inspector General for Education said it investigated the incident and found no evidence of racial bias. It said the Omnilert system perceived the student’s hand movement as a potential threat. “In the Kenwood event, the Omnilert system did not detect a single blue potato chip bag as a threat. The perceived threat was based on the student’s hand movement, including its position and angle,” the report states. The lawsuit describes the incident as “terrifying” for the teens, who feared for their lives and the lives of their friends. It alleges that one of the officers present thanked the teens for not running away, underscoring the dangers Black people face during encounters with law enforcement. The lawsuit further alleges that the school’s principal joked about the situation in a text to administrators, writing, “It was a bag of chips” with four crying-laughing emojis. One of the teens is still a student at Kenwood and the others are in college. “The police told my son this could have been a real problem,” Freida Winfield, the parent of one of the teens, said in a statement. “No child in Baltimore County should face this kind of danger while waiting outside his own school for a ride home from his mother.”

articles.title: Israeli military launches rare ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line
articles.summary: Hamas condemns the incursion, which the Israeli military says is dismantling a "terror tunnel", as a "flagrant" ceasefire violation.
articles.body:
Israeli ground forces have launched a rare operation in part of the central Gaza Strip outside their control, after issuing evacuation orders for residents.

Witnesses said tanks advanced east of Nuseirat refugee camp and rolled onto the territory's main north to south road under the cover of artillery strikes.

The Israeli military said the "targeted" operation aimed to dismantle a "terror tunnel" west of the so-called Yellow Line, which marks the more than 60% of Gaza's territory occupied by Israel.

The Palestinian armed group Hamas, which controls the rest of Gaza, accused Israel of a "flagrant violation" of the October 2025 ceasefire agreement.

Violence has continued in Gaza over the past 13 months, with near-daily Israeli strikes, and living conditions for the 2.1 million people there remain dire.

Early on Wednesday afternoon, Israeli military body Cogat's Arabic spokesperson announced the start of the incursion and warned Palestinians living in an area north of Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camp to stay away for their own safety.

It also said a section of the north to south Salah al-Din road that passed through the area would be closed to traffic.

Later, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it had begun a joint operation with the Shin Bet security service "to dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to IDF troops".

"IDF troops under the Southern Command are deployed in the area in accordance with the ceasefire agreement and will continue to operate to remove any immediate threat and thwart attempts by the Hamas terrorist organisation to harm Israeli civilians or IDF troops, or to violate the agreement," it added.

Hamas warned in a statement that the advance of Israeli military vehicles beyond the Yellow Line and the evacuation of residents constituted "a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement".

Footage published by Palestinian media outlets and on social media showed families fleeing areas near Nuseirat camp following the announcement.

In one video verified by BBC Verify, a man can be seen ducking after hearing artillery fire and then running along Salah al-Din road, about 1.5km (0.9 miles) west of the Yellow Line. "The Israeli occupation now is firing randomly near the houses and tents of people," he says.

Automatic gunfire can be heard in another video filmed just to the south-east.

A resident of Nuseirat who was forced to flee told BBC Arabic's Middle East Daily programme: "The situation is now extremely dire, with Israeli forces firing indiscriminately at areas where displaced people have sought shelter."

"We couldn't take any of our belongings with us - not even our blankets, pillows, or clothes. We had no choice but to leave everything behind."

A second resident also reported "indiscriminate gunfire and shelling" and said there had been "numerous casualties, including fatalities".

Asked about reported fatalities, the IDF sent a general statement about the operation.

Israel building new land barriers in Gaza and displacing families

Israel moves Yellow Line deeper into Gaza, satellite images show

Gaza's Hamas-run Civil Defence agency said three people were killed and others were wounded in three separate Israeli drone strikes on Wednesday.

One man was killed in Nuseirat, the second to the north in Gaza City, and the third in the central town of Deir al-Balah, it added.

The IDF told the BBC that it had "struck several military operatives".

At least 1,658 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the ceasefire began last year, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

The Israeli military says six of its soldiers have been killed over the same period.

Meanwhile, more than 1.9 million people - about 90% of Gaza's population - remain displaced, with 1.4 million of them living in tents or makeshift shelters, according to the UN.

Reconstruction has yet to begin in Gaza, where an estimated 82% of all structures have been destroyed or damaged during the war, as US President Donald Trump's peace plan has largely stalled.

The disarmament of Hamas has been a key sticking point.

The group has agreed to give up its weapons in exchange for a phased withdrawal of Israeli troops from the 60% of Gaza they currently occupy. But Israel has insisted that Hamas must fully disarm before any pullout.

The war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Since then, more than 74,700 people have been killed in Gaza, the health ministry says.

articles.title: SC starts contempt case against lawyer for remarks against CJI
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: SC Wednesday initiated contempt proceedings against advocate Pravin Singhal for making derogatory remarks against CJI Surya Kant while
articles.body: NEW DELHI: SC Wednesday initiated contempt proceedings against advocate Pravin Singhal for making derogatory remarks against CJI Surya Kant while appearing before his bench on Nov 16.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta, Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed the erring lawyer to file his response by Jan 8 and also ordered him to appear personally before it on the next date of hearing on Jan 20."Having perused the papers placed before us, which includes the requisite consent of the learned Attorney General for India under Section 15(1)(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, we are prima facie satisfied that the motion made by the petitioner - Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) - for initiation of proceedings against the sole respondent / alleged contemnor for the alleged derogatory remarks referred to in the petition together with the attempt to scandalise the authority of the Court deserves to be taken forward," the bench said in its order.The controversy arose after the lawyer, aggrieved by an alleged procedural lapse in non-listing of a petition, questioned the integrity of the CJI in open court proceedings and went to extent of telling him "You cannot sit in that chair. You do not deserve. You do not have the integrity for that."Taking strong exception to the lawyer's scandalous behaviour, SCBA took the initiative to kick off the process against the lawyer. It first approached attorney general to take his consent which is needed to file a contempt petition. After getting his approval, the petition was drafted and filed and the court also showed the urgency to immediately list the case.SCBA president and senior advocate Pradeep Rai said that the court must deal with such people with an iron hand as such incidents keep happening. "They feel that no action can be taken against them and that they can keep doing this. There must be a strict procedure. We have to deal with these situations with an iron hand," he said.Expressing concern over such incidents happening inside a courtroom, former judges of HCs - T Raja, Sudhir Saxena, S K Gangele - issued a statement saying: "Judiciary is the only hope of one hundred & forty seven crores of people, therefore the trust & hopes of people can't be compromised by allowing vested interests to malign this institution with calculated conspiracy. Senior members of legal fraternity can't be silent spectators to frequent attacks on judiciary."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
